summary: Rename Django User.note to customer_note while keeping the public GraphQL field note, using bidirectional column sync triggers to guarantee read consistency across old and new app versions during a staged migration.
write_consistency: Add customer_note column, backfill data from note, and create two BEFORE INSERT/UPDATE triggers: one copies note → customer_note, the other copies customer_note → note. This ensures whichever version writes a value, the other version can read it from its known column. After retire_old, the note column is dropped and customer_note holds the latest value written by either version.
revision_notes: Root cause: the previous plan only added a one‑way trigger (note → customer_note). This caused failures when the new version wrote customer_note (old could not see it), when new created rows (old read null), and when clears were silently restored. Adding a reverse trigger (customer_note → note) makes writes from either direction visible to the other version and propagates clears bidirectionally.

stages.description: Add customer_note column, backfill data from note, and add bidirectional sync triggers.
sql: ALTER TABLE account_user ADD COLUMN customer_note TEXT NULL;
UPDATE account_user SET customer_note = note WHERE note IS NOT NULL;
CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION sync_note_to_customer() RETURNS TRIGGER AS $$ BEGIN NEW.customer_note := COALESCE(NEW.customer_note, NEW.note); RETURN NEW; END; $$ LANGUAGE plpgsql;
CREATE TRIGGER sync_note_to_customer_trg BEFORE INSERT OR UPDATE ON account_user FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION sync_note_to_customer();
CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION sync_customer_to_note() RETURNS TRIGGER AS $$ BEGIN NEW.note := COALESCE(NEW.note, NEW.customer_note); RETURN NEW; END; $$ LANGUAGE plpgsql;
CREATE TRIGGER sync_customer_to_note_trg BEFORE INSERT OR UPDATE ON account_user FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION sync_customer_to_note();

stages.description: Deploy the new application version (new-staged) which uses the customer_note column exclusively. Code changes (model field, resolvers, bulk mutates, anonymization) have already been applied per investigator findings.
Retire the old application version (old) that writes to the note column. Traffic is shifted to the new version only.
Remove the now-unused note column after the old version is retired, leaving only customer_note.
sql: ALTER TABLE account_user DROP COLUMN note;
